coverage: All eight local sections: banquet and framing speakers, named cultural and family references, explicit servant roles and imagined figures; exclusions for translator titles and missing opening frame.

entities.name: Socrates
entities.body: The Athenian philosopher attending Agathon’s banquet.

entities.name: Apollodorus
entities.body: The narrator retelling the banquet conversation from Aristodemus’s account.

entities.name: Aristodemus
entities.body: Socrates’ companion at the banquet, whose eyewitness account Apollodorus retells.

entities.name: Agathon
entities.body: The tragic playwright hosting the banquet to celebrate his victory.

entities.name: Phaedrus
entities.body: The guest whose wish to hear Love praised inspires the evening’s speeches.

entities.name: Pausanias
entities.body: Agathon’s lover and one of the guests giving a speech about love.

entities.name: Eryximachus
entities.body: The physician at the banquet, son of Acumenus, who proposes the order of speeches.

entities.name: Aristophanes
entities.body: The comic playwright attending Agathon’s banquet.

entities.name: Diotima
entities.body: The wise woman from Mantineia whose teaching about love Socrates recounts.

entities.name: Alcibiades
entities.body: The Athenian statesman and commander, an admirer of Socrates, who joins the banquet.

entities.name: Apollodorus’s listener
entities.body: The unnamed companion asking Apollodorus to retell the banquet conversation.

entities.name: Acumenus
entities.body: Eryximachus’s father, also a physician.

entities.name: Homer
entities.body: The ancient Greek epic poet repeatedly cited by the speakers.

entities.name: Euripides
entities.body: The Athenian tragic playwright quoted by the guests.

entities.name: Prodicus
entities.body: The sophist recalled for his prose treatment of Heracles.

entities.name: Hesiod
entities.body: The Greek poet whose account of the gods’ beginnings is cited.

entities.name: Parmenides
entities.body: The Greek philosopher and poet cited on the origins of Love.

entities.name: Acusilaus
entities.body: The early Greek prose writer who recorded myths and genealogies.

entities.name: Aeschylus
entities.body: The Athenian tragic playwright whose depiction of Achilles and Patroclus is disputed by Phaedrus.

entities.name: Aristogeiton
entities.body: The Athenian associated with Harmodius in the opposition to tyranny.

entities.name: Harmodius
entities.body: The Athenian associated with Aristogeiton in the opposition to tyranny.

entities.name: Heraclitus
entities.body: The Greek philosopher cited for harmony arising from opposing forces.

entities.name: Gorgias
entities.body: The celebrated teacher of rhetoric invoked in Socrates’ wordplay about Agathon’s speech.

entities.name: Lycurgus
entities.body: The traditional Spartan lawgiver, cited for the lasting value of his laws.

entities.name: Solon
entities.body: The Athenian lawgiver cited among creators of lasting civic achievements.

entities.name: Olympus
entities.body: The legendary flute musician associated with Marsyas, whose melodies Alcibiades discusses.

entities.name: Pericles
entities.body: The Athenian statesman and orator whom Alcibiades compares with Socrates.

entities.name: Laches
entities.body: The Athenian soldier and commander who retreats beside Socrates at Delium in Alcibiades’ account.

entities.name: Brasidas
entities.body: The Spartan commander used as an example of heroic courage.

entities.name: Charmides
entities.body: The son of Glaucon whom Alcibiades names among those drawn to Socrates.

entities.name: Glaucon
entities.body: Charmides’ father, named in Alcibiades’ account.

entities.name: Euthydemus
entities.body: The son of Diocles whom Alcibiades names among Socrates’ admirers.

entities.name: Diocles
entities.body: The father of Euthydemus.

entities.name: Aristotle
entities.body: The Greek philosopher cited in the translator’s references to the Politics.

entities.name: Alexander Pope
entities.body: The English poet whose translation of Homer supplies the quoted line.

entities.name: Agamemnon
entities.body: The commander of the Greek army at Troy, Menelaus’s brother.

entities.name: Menelaus
entities.body: The Greek king of Sparta and brother of Agamemnon in the Homeric comparison.

entities.name: Dionysus
entities.body: The Greek god of wine and theater, invoked as judge of the poets’ and speakers’ contest.

entities.name: Melanippe
entities.body: The mythological heroine whose words in a play by Euripides Eryximachus borrows.

entities.name: Eros (Love)
entities.body: The figure of Love whose nature and power the guests debate.

entities.name: Heracles
entities.body: The Greek hero recalled in Prodicus’s moral tale and in Alcibiades’ exclamation.

entities.name: Aphrodite
entities.body: The Greek goddess of love and beauty.

entities.name: Chaos
entities.body: The primordial void in Hesiod’s account of the beginnings of the gods.

entities.name: Earth
entities.body: The primordial Earth, or Gaia, in the quoted account of the gods’ beginnings.

entities.name: Alcestis
entities.body: The wife of Admetus and daughter of Pelias, offered as an example of devoted love.

entities.name: Pelias
entities.body: Alcestis’s father, a king in Greek myth.

entities.name: Admetus
entities.body: Alcestis’s husband in the myth recalled by the speakers.

entities.name: Orpheus
entities.body: The mythical singer who seeks his wife in the underworld.

entities.name: Oeagrus
entities.body: Orpheus’s father.

entities.name: Eurydice
entities.body: Orpheus’s wife, whom he seeks in the underworld.

entities.name: Achilles
entities.body: The Greek hero of the Iliad, companion of Patroclus.

entities.name: Patroclus
entities.body: Achilles’ companion in the Iliad, whom Phaedrus describes as his lover.

entities.name: Thetis
entities.body: Achilles’ mother, the sea goddess who tells him of his possible fates.

entities.name: Hector
entities.body: The Trojan hero opposed to Achilles in the Iliad.

entities.name: Uranus
entities.body: The primordial sky god, father of the heavenly Aphrodite in Pausanias’s account.

entities.name: Zeus
entities.body: The chief Olympian god in the stories and comparisons told by the guests.

entities.name: Dione
entities.body: The goddess named with Zeus as the parent of the common Aphrodite.

entities.name: Asclepius
entities.body: The Greek god of healing, whom Eryximachus credits with founding medicine.

entities.name: Urania
entities.body: The heavenly Muse in Eryximachus’s comparison of kinds of musical love.

entities.name: Polyhymnia
entities.body: The Muse contrasted with Urania in Eryximachus’s account of music and love.

entities.name: Otus
entities.body: The giant called Otys, who with Ephialtes attempts to reach the gods.

entities.name: Ephialtes
entities.body: The giant paired with Otus in the assault on heaven.

entities.name: Apollo
entities.body: The Greek god who helps reshape humans in Aristophanes’ myth, also associated with healing and prophecy.

entities.name: Hephaestus
entities.body: The divine smith whom Aristophanes imagines offering to join lovers permanently.

entities.name: Iapetus
entities.body: The Titan invoked as an example of a very ancient god.

entities.name: Kronos
entities.body: The Titan who is Zeus’s father, invoked in the account of the older gods.

entities.name: Necessity
entities.body: The personified force to which Agathon attributes the old conflicts among the gods.

entities.name: Ate
entities.body: The goddess of delusion and ruin, quoted as an example of delicacy in Homer.

entities.name: Ares
entities.body: The Greek god of war, described as mastered by love for Aphrodite.

entities.name: The Muses
entities.body: The goddesses of music and poetry.

entities.name: Athena
entities.body: The Greek goddess associated with weaving, called Athene here.

entities.name: The Gorgon
entities.body: The petrifying monster evoked by Socrates’ joke about Gorgias’s rhetoric.

entities.name: Poros (Plenty)
entities.body: The personification of resourcefulness, son of Metis, in Diotima’s story of Love’s birth.

entities.name: Metis (Discretion)
entities.body: The personification of wisdom and resourceful thought, Poros’s mother in Diotima’s story.

entities.name: Penia (Poverty)
entities.body: The personification of poverty in Diotima’s story of Love’s birth.

entities.name: Codrus
entities.body: The legendary Athenian king cited as an example of self-sacrifice for lasting fame.

entities.name: Poseidon
entities.body: The Greek god of the sea, invoked by Alcibiades.

entities.name: Silenus
entities.body: The satyr-like figure whose hollow statuettes Alcibiades compares with Socrates.

entities.name: Marsyas
entities.body: The mythical satyr and flute-player whose musical power is compared with Socrates’ speech.

entities.name: Diomedes
entities.body: The Greek hero called Diomede, recalled for exchanging bronze armor for gold in the Iliad.

entities.name: Ajax
entities.body: The mighty Greek hero of the Trojan War, used as a comparison for resistance to injury.

entities.name: Nestor
entities.body: The elderly Greek king renowned for wise speech in Homer.

entities.name: Antenor
entities.body: The Trojan elder and counselor compared with Pericles for his eloquence.

entities.name: The divine
entities.body: A general reference to gods and divine power in the speakers’ discussion.

entities.name: Agathon’s welcoming servant
entities.body: The household servant who brings Aristodemus into the banquet.

entities.name: The servant sent for Socrates
entities.body: The attendant who reports Socrates standing absorbed in the neighboring portico.

entities.name: Agathon’s servants
entities.body: The household attendants serving the banquet.

entities.name: The banquet flute-player
entities.body: The female musician present before the guests begin their speeches.

entities.name: Alcibiades’ flute-player
entities.body: The female musician accompanying Alcibiades on his arrival.

entities.name: Alcibiades’ attendants
entities.body: The companions helping Alcibiades into the banquet.

entities.name: The late revelers
entities.body: The group that enters Agathon’s house near the end of the night.

entities.name: Admetus’s parents
entities.body: The father and mother contrasted with Alcestis in Phaedrus’s example of devotion.

entities.name: The original humans
entities.body: The double-bodied ancestors in Aristophanes’ invented account of human love.
